subject: Low-latency safeguard for Dedicated Pool / SLA language
messages:
From: Aisha Mathews <aisha@brightlynx.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool: request for low-latency safeguard

Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. BrightLynx is close to selecting a provider for our inference tier; we like Redwood's telemetry and billing model. One outstanding ask from our infra/ops team: we need a documented safeguard for tail latency on dedicated pools for our customer-facing scoring calls. Details below: 

- Traffic profile: steady-state 30k qps distributed across 20k users; typical inference request <= 512 tokens; spiky bursts at EOD and during weekly batch jobs.
- Requirement: p99 latency <= 200ms for non-batched inference requests under expected load; while we understand occasional spikes happen, we need a predictable mitigation (priority lane, pre-allocated headroom, or credits) for production-impacting tail events.
- Contract ask: either an engineering mitigation (hard priority queue + gated concurrency) or a monthly credit band tied to p99 breaches.

I've attached our Service-Profile CSV with traffic slices and RL-based retry behavior we run on the client. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to a latency safeguard, and what options/options pricing would look like? We'd like to finalize SLA language as part of the BLYX-438 procurement flow.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

Aisha Mathews
Head of Platform Reliability
BrightLynx
Attachment: Service-Profile-BrightLynx.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mathews <aisha@brightlynx.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool: request for low-latency safeguard

Aisha —

Appreciate the clear profile and the file. Looping in Vanessa (sales lead) and Rishi (infrastructure) to propose concrete options. High level, there are three routes we can propose: 

1) Priority lane + reserved headroom: carve out a concurrency/slot band inside the dedicated pool that bypasses batching and gets scheduled ahead of best-effort work. Requires 10–20% additional reserved capacity.
2) Aggressive tail SLO with credits: define a p99 latency SLO and a credit calculation for monthly breaches (we can draft the formula).
3) Hybrid: priority lane + a smaller credit band for operational anomalies.

Two quick questions for BrightLynx: 1) what fraction of your traffic must meet the p99 <=200ms constraint (all production vs subset), and 2) will you accept a token/length bound (e.g., requests <=512 tokens) for the SLO? These boundaries materially change engineering risk.

Vanessa/Rishi — can you please weigh in on feasibility, expected cost uplift, and a recommended fallback policy (model variant fallback or pause/queueing behavior) we should include? If this looks feasible, I'll ask Legal/Finance to prep language and get Procurement into the loop.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Thanks — putting a short commercial note here so Aisha has visibility: 

- Customer ask: p99 <=200ms on dedicated pool for production traffic (token cap 512), plus mitigation when we see p99 breaches.
- Commercial approach: priority lane + reserved headroom (recommended) typically maps to ~15% capacity uplift on top of committed GPUs. For customers who prefer not to provision extra GPUs, we offer a credit model where monthly credits are paid when p99 breaches exceed the agreed threshold.
- Pricing: rough uplift estimate is an annual add-on equal to ~12–18% of committed spend for priority lane (final number depends on model size and expected concurrency).

I've attached a quick config-options sheet that summarizes trade-offs (preemptible nodes, non-preemptible headroom, per-customer priority queue). Internal note: we should flag whether priority lanes require kernel scheduling changes for certain quantized runtimes — Rishi?

Next step: Rishi, can you confirm engineering constraints and draft a short SLA paragraph we can present to BrightLynx legal. Aisha — if you can confirm whether this must apply to 100% of production traffic or a smaller slice, that will speed things up.

-Vanessa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachment: config-options.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

On Fri, Aug 21, 2026 at 9:17 AM Aisha Mathews <aisha@brightlynx.com> wrote:
> Karthik —
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week. BrightLynx is close to selecting a provider for our inference tier; we like Redwood's telemetry and billing model. One outstanding ask from our infra/ops team: we need a documented safeguard for tail latency on dedicated pools for our customer-facing scoring calls.
> 
> - Traffic profile: steady-state 30k qps distributed across 20k users; typical inference request <= 512 tokens; spiky bursts at EOD and during weekly batch jobs.
> - Requirement: p99 latency <= 200ms for non-batched inference requests under expected load; while we understand occasional spikes happen, we need a predictable mitigation (priority lane, pre-allocated headroom, or credits) for production-impacting tail events.

Thanks for the details — I looked through the attached CSV and the traffic slices. Short summary from infra: 

- Feasibility: We can offer a service-level construct that provides a low-latency "priority lane" inside a dedicated pool. With KV-prefix caching, request-level throttles, and a small reserved headroom (we recommend 1.5x typical concurrency), we can meet p99 <=200ms for requests <=512 tokens under 95% utilization for that customer's reserved slice.
- Engineering caveats: the guarantee requires (a) a model variant that does not trigger heavy memory compaction on high concurrency (we recommend quantized-8 or dynamic-quant approach), (b) no model hot-swapping during observation windows, and (c) limited background batch jobs on nodes that host the priority lane.
- Fallbacks: propose automatic fallback to a slightly lower-cost compatible model variant (latency upper bound documented) if headroom is exhausted, and an automatic crediting rule for measurable p99 breaches.

I've drafted proposed SLA language below (please review):

"Redwood will maintain a Monthly Latency SLO for the Dedicated Slice provisioned by the Customer as follows: For qualifying requests (inference requests <=512 tokens to approved model variants routed through the Customer's Dedicated Slice during Redwood's monitoring intervals), Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure p99 latency <=200ms. If Redwood fails to meet this SLO in a given monthly period, the Customer will be eligible for Service Credits equal to X% of the monthly committed fee for each 0.5% of SLO shortfall beyond a 1% tolerance band, up to a cap of Y% per month. The SLO excludes scheduled maintenance, force majeure, and operationally necessary model rollouts."

Action items: 
1) Sales to confirm whether BrightLynx wants this applied to 100% of prod traffic or a named subset.
2) Finance/Legal to vet the credit formula (X/Y placeholders) and confirm commercial cap.
3) Product to confirm whether kernel-level scheduling changes are required for specific model and quantization combos; if so, we'll add a deployment notice term.

I'm happy to review the SLA language with our legal team and produce a redline. If BrightLynx agrees in principle, we can attach the SLA as an addendum to the Dedicated Capacity agreement and move to DocuSign (link below).

DocuSign sandbox: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/BLYX-438-SLA

-Rishi
Staff/Lead, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
